sensory.aromaNotes: Apricot / dried-fruit aroma with a mild pepper finish; used as a culinary flavor, not a neutral analog base
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Ectomycorrhizal; not industrially cultivated at protein scale. Chewy fruiting bodies can add bite in blends, but the realistic alt-protein role is aroma/umami, not bulk mycoprotein. True chanterelles have ridges (false gills), not oyster-style shreddable lamellae.
sensory.preparationContext: Wild or woodland-harvested fruiting bodies, sautéed or dried; cultivation remains unreliable
sensory.confidenceNotes: Flavor chemistry is documented in edible-mushroom reviews. No commercial meat-analog product is built on C. cibarius biomass.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: Funnel-shaped pileus with blunt, forked ridges (not true gills) running down a solid stipe
morphology.sporeCharacteristics: Pale yellow to cream spore print
morphology.microscopyNotes: Ridges are folds of hymenium, not detachable lamellae

nutrition.preparationContext: Typical wild-chanterelle proximate ranges from edible-mushroom reviews (dry-matter protein often cited ~15–25%)
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Composition varies by site and drying. Not a formulation protein spec.

geographic.cultivatedRegions: Not a reliable industrial crop; mostly wild harvest and limited experimental culture

strains.availabilityNotes: Mycorrhizal; culture collections hold isolates, not a production strain.

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Gourmet wild mushroom sold fresh or dried. In alt-protein it is a flavor/texture accent (apricot, pepper, chew), not a scalable analog base.
commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Traditional food; not a mycoprotein platform.

regulatory.notes: Traditional wild edible. Confirm local look-alike warnings (false chanterelles) for any consumer product.

altProteinResearch.title: Edible mushrooms: chemical composition and nutritional value
altProteinResearch.summary: Places chanterelles among wild edibles with documented aroma and proximate composition — flavor adjuncts, not industrial protein biomass.
